changelog: Replace O2 with an order rule that prefers the later cut which preserves a fronted adjunct over an earlier cut that fragments it — directly addresses the primary 'fronted adjunct' finding.
findings: When two candidate cuts both lie inside the same fronted adjunct, the prompt often prefers an earlier split that fragments the adjunct; the better choice preserves the adjunct as a unit attached to the clause that follows.

The prompt permits cuts that sever an initial subordinate/adverbial/preposed phrase from the sentence's main finite predicate, producing left fragments that lose scope or contradict the whole sentence.

diagnosis.why: The O2 replacement made the scorer prefer the later cut that preserves a fronted adjunct, so cuts were pushed later and the top-of-list choices at shallow depths shifted into deeper ranks. That produced gains for short-latency bins (≤3–7 pieces) which keep many candidates (rank-depth coincidence improved at deeper depths) but slightly reduced top-1 precision and produced a small loss for the longest bin (≤99).
diagnosis.lesson: When preferring later cuts to keep fronted adjuncts intact, retain or recover precision for the very top ranks so long-latency budgets (which rely on the first one or two positions) are not harmed.
